children: , the cybersecurity platform provider, fell 2.69% to $243.69 at 10:10 a.m. ET on November 2, even as Deutsche Bank upgraded the company to Buy from Hold and lifted its price target to $300 from $240. The bet centers on rising demand for AI security. The challenge is turning that demand into paying customers, recurring revenue and cash.

CrowdStrike's August 26 results put annual recurring revenue at $5.84 billion, up 25%, with quarterly revenue of approximately $1.47 billion and free cash flow of $377.4 million. That translates into a roughly 25.7% free-cash-flow margina useful measure of how much revenue reaches the cash register after capital spending. Management's next-quarter ARR guidance of $6.1844 billion to $6.1884 billion implies approximately 5.9% sequential growth at the midpoint, giving investors a concrete benchmark for the AI-security pitch.

The GuruFocus snapshot adds a valuation checkpoint: a GF Score of 72/100, with growth the strongest spoke and GF Value the weakest. That combination suggests business expansion could remain compelling while the valuation leaves less room for disappointment. The next test is execution: CrowdStrike needs to sustain recurring-revenue growth while protecting cash conversion. A bigger security market may create opportunity, but customer commitments and cash generation will determine how much of it reaches shareholders.

title: CrowdStrike Stocks Decline 2.7% With Upgrade Testing AI Security Revenue Conversion
